articles.title: 'Westminster is not working': Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland unite against UK rule
articles.description: Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland have signed a new cooperation agreement described as an “independence pact,” intensifying debate over the future of the United Kingdom. The agreement calls for closer cooperation among nationalist movements and urges Westminster to prepare for constitutional change. Scotland’s John Swinney highlighted renewed demands for an independence referendum, while Wales’ Rhun ap Iorwerth argued that Westminster is failing to serve the nations effectively. Northern Ireland’s Michelle O’Neill and Sinn Fein leader Mary Lou McDonald also backed the right to self-determination. The development follows Donald Trump’s recent comments supporting Irish reunification, adding fresh pressure to an already sensitive constitutional debate.

articles.title: MBS’ first message to the Houthis? Saudi Air Force flexes its might after major Red Sea humiliation

The display comes as Yemen’s Houthis reportedly make rapid advances along the Red Sea coast, including claims surrounding Mocha and Perim Island. Riyadh’s message describes Saudi Arabia as a “fortress of might” and a shield of national security. Is the video simply a patriotic military showcase — or a warning to the Houthis and their backers? As tensions rise across the Red Sea and Yemen, Saudi air power could become increasingly important. Here’s what Riyadh’s latest show of force could signal.

articles.title: MBS arm-twists Trump for help as Houthis rain missiles on Saudi: US says no, offers this instead...
articles.description: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has held talks with U.S. Central Command chief Admiral Brad Cooper in Jeddah amid escalating Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia. The Saudi Press Agency said the meeting reviewed Saudi-U.S. relations and the latest regional developments. It came days after the crown prince reportedly asked President Donald Trump for direct U.S. military action against Yemen’s Houthi movement. Reuters reported that Washington declined to take direct military action for now, but agreed to support Riyadh with intelligence-sharing and targeting assistance. The U.S. support is also reported to include advice on Saudi air-defence strategy as the kingdom faces continuing aerial threats to cities, energy sites and key Red Sea approaches.
